title: Textile Map
description: A schematic tile map of the eight countries of South Asia with ten dots for famous textiles and garments: Jamdani, ajrak, the perahan tunban, Kashmir pashmina, Chyangra Pashmina, Bhutanese kira weaving, Banarasi silk, ikat, Kanjivaram silk and the Kandyan osariya. Learners see each one's place, fiber and technique with a garment drawing and a procedural pattern swatch, then test themselves in a quiz mode.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Textiles
Clothing
Weaving and dyeing
Geography of craft
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Connect ten South Asian textiles and garments to the regions where they are made.
Identify the fiber (cotton, silk or wool) used in each textile.
Explain the difference between patterns woven in (Jamdani, brocade), dyed into the thread before weaving (ikat) and printed on (ajrak).
prerequisites: Knowing the eight countries of South Asia (Chapter 1)
Knowing that cloth is woven from warp and weft threads
keyQuestions: Where are Jamdani, ajrak, ikat and Kanjivaram made?
Why does pashmina come from high mountain regions?
How is a woven pattern different from a tie-dyed or block-printed one?
misconceptions: Every South Asian textile pattern is printed onto the cloth.
Pashmina is a brand name rather than a fiber from Himalayan goats.
A garment always tells you which country someone is from.
